## Design

### 2026-10-07 – 1. Looked at the GitHub repo

**6h**

1. Looked at the GitHub repo

2. Downloaded KiCad
   I downloaded and installed KiCad so I could start working on the project.

3. Watched KiCad tutorials
   I watched several tutorials to learn how to use KiCad, as I had not used it much before.

4. Set up the libraries and footprints
   I had some trouble getting the footprints and libraries working correctly. I did a lot of troubleshooting and followed the same folder and library setup used in the GitHub repository.

5. Worked on the schematic
   I started working on the schematic editor and added and connected the different components.

6. Worked on the PCB
   I moved on to the PCB editor. This was one of the harder parts for me because I was still learning how KiCad worked.

7. Created the Starbie board shape
   Making the Starbie-shaped PCB was difficult. I opened the original Starbie project file and used its board shape because it looked much better than the shape I was able to make myself.

8. Worked on the BOM
   I then worked on the Bill of Materials (BOM) and started looking for the components I needed.

9. Looking for cheaper parts
   I am still working on the BOM and trying to find cheaper components. This has been difficult because electronic components and shipping can be quite expensive in Sydney.

10. Current progress
    I am still working on the project, mainly checking the BOM and trying to reduce the overall cost.

### 2026-10-09 – - Worked further on the PCB design in KiCad and finalised the PCB files.

**10h**

- Worked further on the PCB design in KiCad and finalised the PCB files.
- Generated the Gerber and drill (DRL) files for PCB manufacturing.
- Created the GitHub repository to organise and document the project files.
- Customised the original firmware by adding new features and interactive behaviours to make Starbie more engaging.
- Added weather-based reactions, including sweating in hot weather, shivering in cold weather, and rain effects in humid conditions.
- Added new animations and behaviours, including tilt-based gravity, looking around, hopping, humming, and chasing bugs.
- Developed a catch game where the player tilts the board to catch apples and avoid obstacles, with three lives, a saved high score, and rewards that affect Starbie's joy and food.
- Improved the display refresh rate for smoother animations.
- Modified Button 2 so that a quick press displays Starbie's stats when the button is released.
- Finalised the Bill of Materials (BOM), including component details and estimated costs.
- Fixed remaining issues and reviewed the project files to finalise the design.
- Reviewed the firmware for syntax errors in the IDE. However, I could not fully compile or test the code on the actual hardware because the components have not arrived yet. The firmware's behaviour therefore remains unverified on the physical device.
